title: New Publication in Global Ecology and Biogeography
text: Led by Dr. Gao, this study compiled over 5,000 soil samples globally using amplicon and metagenomic sequencing across multiple trophic levels (archaea, bacteria, fungi, protists, and invertebrates). Key finding: multitrophic soil biodiversity deviates from the classical latitudinal diversity gradient—most taxa show no decline in diversity towards the poles. Instead, local soil properties (pH, carbon, nitrogen) and climate override latitude in shaping biodiversity patterns. The work challenges the universality of the LDG and highlights the dominant role of environmental filtering over biogeographic history in soil communities.
